cues.en: What's the fastest way to board an airplane? I mean, you can't just throw open the gates like funneling cattle into a chute. That's not for us. We're primates, after all. So let's put our monkey brains to work to tackle this cue, which is what boarding groups do. Prioritize plainly packing primates precisely. Eh, primarily.
cues.zh: 登机最快的方式是什么？总不能像把牛赶进围栏那样直接敞开闸门吧。那可不是我们人类的风格。毕竟我们是灵长类动物。所以让我们动动“猴脑”来解决这个问题——登机组干的就是这个事：清晰优先、精准有序地安排灵长类排队登机。大概吧。

cues.en: Okay, we have a suggestion. Pour people into the plane back to front. This is an intuitive solution to fill a cylinder. But there's almost a law of the universe that solutions which are the first thing you think of and look sensible and are easy to implement are often terrible, ineffective solutions once implemented will drag on civilization forever. Cough. Voting systems. Cough. So it should come as no surprise that this method is
cues.zh: 好，我们有一个建议：让人们从后往前灌进飞机。这是填充一个圆筒的直观方案。但几乎有一条宇宙法则：那些最先想到、看起来合理、又容易实现的方案，往往在实施后糟糕透顶、效率低下，还会拖累文明 forever。咳咳，投票制度。咳咳。所以毫不意外，这种方法

cues.en: not good, and also what most airlines use to board their planes. Let's watch it in action. The first boarding group walks to the back of the plane. Everything is smooth, right until the first to go reaches their row and starts to stow. So slow. And for passenger too, while their seat is in view, there's nothing to do. The aisle's one queue, where all cannot but stew stuck like glue until this guy's through. Phew. It's bags. Bags cause most of the delay. Boarding.
cues.zh: 效果不佳，而且它恰恰是大多数航空公司使用的登机方式。我们来看看它的实际表现。第一登机组走向机舱后部。一切都很顺利，直到第一个到达座位的人开始放行李。太慢了。对后面的乘客也一样，明明看得到自己的座位，却什么也做不了。过道就是一条队，所有人只能干着急，像被胶水粘住一样，直到这家伙搞定。呼。都是行李。行李造成了大部分延误。登机

cues.en: flight. Like with this, a full stop stow. When it happens, everyone boarding the plane within and without must wait until one person finishes stowing their bag. Can you feel it? The aggregate lost seconds of human life piling up like a bounty for a delighted reaper? Of course you can. You can feel it with every bag.
cues.zh: 航班。比如这种：完全停止放行李。一旦发生，机舱内外所有正在登机的人，都必须等一个人放完行李。你能感受到吗？那些累积起来浪费的人类生命秒数，像赏金一样堆给死神收割？当然能。每一个行李箱你都能感受到。

cues.en: What was I saying? Right, back to front boarding groups have a lot of full stop stows and very few of what you want. Pullaways and parallels and parallels and pullaways. Pullaways turn one cue into two and parallels decrease total bagged stow time and are super satisfying. The rare triple partner parallel invoking a double high five at the sheer pleasure of its efficiency. But loading back to front lets few of these happen. Now, say you weren't just not good
cues.zh: 我刚说到哪了？对，从后往前的登机组会产生大量完全停止放行李，而很少有我们想要的情况：拉开并行、并行拉开。拉开把一条队变成两条，并行则减少总放行李时间，而且超级令人满足。罕见的三人并行，其效率带来的愉悦甚至能触发双重击掌。但从后往前装载几乎不会让这些发生。现在，假设你不只是不擅长

cues.en: at designing boarding groups, but you were malicious and wanted to maximize the amount of human life wasted on a flight. What would you do? Not back to front, but front to back. The smaller the boarding group, the better. This makes almost every tedious shuffle forward result in a full stop stow because most of the line waits by rows already full or outside the plane. Look familiar? This is where we acknowledge the class structure of airplanes.
cues.zh: 设计登机组，而是心怀恶意，想让一次航班浪费的人类生命最大化。你会怎么做？不是从后往前，而是从前往后。登机组越小越好。这样几乎每一次向前挪动都会导致一次完全停止放行李，因为队伍大多数人都在已坐满的排附近等，或者在飞机外面。眼熟吗？现在是时候承认飞机的阶级结构了。

cues.en: Real planes look like this, and first-class boards first, front to back, before the pro-economy file in back to front. So, excluding pre-boarding, all airlines start with a little of the slowest boarding method you could intentionally design. Now, obviously, this video will soon reveal faster boarding procedures, and you will wonder, why don't airlines use the faster methods? One possible answer is economic incentives.
cues.zh: 真实的飞机是这样的：头等舱先登机，从前往后，然后经济舱乘客才从后往前排队。所以， excluding 预先登机，所有航空公司都先用上一点你能刻意设计出的最慢登机方法。显然，这个视频很快会揭示更快的登机流程，你会想问：为什么航空公司不用更快的方法？一个可能的答案是经济激励。

cues.en: First class pays for perks, sometimes breathtaking perks for breathtaking amounts, and boarding first is one of them. Also, airlines give everyone loyalty points that move you up the class structure the more you fly with that airline, which gives airlines another good reason to group people and probably helps explain why they switched away from the older, faster method you won't believe they used to use.
cues.zh: 头等舱花钱买特权，有时是惊人价格换惊人特权，优先登机就是其中之一。另外，航空公司给每个人忠诚度积分，你越常坐这家航司，就越能在会员等级体系里往上爬；这给了航司另一个给人分组的好理由，也大概能解释它们为什么放弃了以前那种更快、但你不会相信它们用过的方法。

cues.en: Doing nothing and having people board the flight in whatever order they show up to get their assigned seat is faster than organizing tidy boarding groups. This is because random people are spread, well, randomly, increasing the chances of pullaways and parallels, unlike the more orderly methods airlines have switched to. Man, it's always frustrating to know that to literally have done nothing would be faster than the something that is done, but surely there's a better boarding group order to be found if we can just subtract malice and add thinking to this problem.
cues.zh: 什么都不做，让乘客按到场顺序登机、各自去找分配好的座位，反而比组织整齐的登机分组更快。因为随机的人分布得——嗯，很随机，增加了错开和并行的机会，而不像航司后来换用的那些更有秩序的方法。唉，知道字面意义上的“什么都不做”会比“做了点什么”更快，总是很让人沮丧；但如果我们能减去恶意、加入思考，肯定能找到一个更好的登机分组顺序。

cues.en: Ah, three groups. Window, middle, aisle, in that order. This is really the same as doing random thrice, one for each column of the craft, but the reason it's a smidge faster is because it eliminates the other source of boarding delay. Seat shuffles. When people board randomly, seat shuffling is going to happen a bunch, and when people spill into the aisle, it slows the queue. Ordering everyone by window, middle, aisle ensures a seat shuffle will never happen.
cues.zh: 啊，三组：靠窗、中间、靠过道，按这个顺序。其实这跟随机三次——对应机舱每一列——是一回事，但它稍微快一点，是因为它消除了另一个登机延误来源：换座挪动。随机登机时，换座挪动会大量发生；当人们堵到过道里，队列就会变慢。按靠窗、中间、靠过道排序，能保证换座挪动永远不会发生。

cues.en: This seems like it should be a big improvement, but when you simulate boarding an aircraft with a ton of real math, rather than just animating it in a dramatically simplified fashion, or do actual experiments, the seat shuffle just isn't a big deal compared to bag stowage. People wrangling their one bag that won't possibly fit or trying to get on board with three bags because they don't think the rules should apply to them, who then also fiddle around with getting their laptops out after stowing them, those kinds of delays count for much more. So, window middle aisle is maybe a smidge faster than
cues.zh: 这看起来应该是个巨大改进，但当你用大量真实数学来模拟登机，而不是只做一个极度简化的动画，或者做真实实验时，和放行李相比，换座挪动根本不算什么。有人折腾自己那件根本塞不进去的包，或者觉得自己不该受规则约束、非要带三件行李上机，放好行李后还要翻腾着拿笔记本，这类延误的影响大得多。所以，靠窗—中间—靠过道也许只比

cues.en: random, which is good, and some airlines use this method, which gets their planes turned around faster than back to front, while still giving them boarding groups to play games with. The vast majority of airlines use either back to front or window middle aisles, so keep an eye out next time you're boarding a flight, or which is happening to you. But can we go farther?
cues.zh: 随机登机稍快一点，这不错；有些航司用这种方法，让飞机周转比从后往前更快，同时还能保留登机分组来玩花样。绝大多数航司用的是从后往前或靠窗—中间—靠过道，所以下次登机时留意一下，或者看看自己正被怎么安排。但我们还能更进一步吗？

cues.en: leaving the real world with its class systems and people and untidiness and smells, ascending to the platonic plane of physics, where cows are spheres and people cellular automaton who will execute instructions perfectly. Here, in the Celestia, what is the theoretically fastest way to board a plane? On this level, here is what's possible.
cues.zh: 离开现实世界——它有等级制度、人、凌乱和气味——升到物理学的柏拉图平面；在那里，牛是球体，人是会完美执行指令的元胞自动机。在这里，在 Celestia，理论上最快的登机方式是什么？在这个层面上，有这些可能。

cues.en: To achieve this ballet, there are no boarding groups, but everyone stands in an exact order, back to front and alternating rows on alternating sides, windows in. This maximizes pull-aways and parallels for steamy packing people in a pinch.
cues.zh: 为了实现这场芭蕾，不分登机组，所有人按精确顺序站好：从后到前，隔排交替、左右交替，靠窗的先入。这样能最大化分流与并行，在拥挤时高效地把人塞进去。

cues.en: Witnessing such glory is too much for mortal minds to bear for long, so we are forced to descend back down into the meat world. The cacophony, the smell, where we must stuff monkeys into a tube. Monkeys with families where separating their young invites chaos and cleanup, where economic incentives divide to profit, and where, even at their best, the human inability to follow instructions is breathtaking.
cues.zh: 目睹这种荣光，凡人头脑撑不了多久，所以我们只能跌回肉身世界。嘈杂、气味，我们得把猴子塞进一根管子里。猴子还有家庭，拆散幼崽会招来混乱和善后；经济激励为了利润把人分开；而即便状态最好，人类不服从指令的程度也令人叹为观止。

cues.en: Here, people upon seeing boarding group 123 would flip the hell out, let alone the impossibility of trying to get them to stand in line in order, and where, even if faster, like watching seconds of a clock, people would complain it was slower. Such gifts we were not meant to have. But is there a way we can modify this perfection to improve our lot on this plane? Yes.
cues.zh: 在这里，人们一看到 123 号登机组就会炸毛，更别说让他们按顺序排队有多不可能；而且就算更快，像看钟表秒针一样，人们也会抱怨更慢。这种礼物本就不是给我们准备的。但有没有办法把这份完美改造一下，改善我们在这架飞机上的处境？有。

cues.en: Instead of exact order, boarding group the first would be all one side of the plane in every other row. Boarding group the second, the other side, then back, and back again. One, two, three, four. We can't ask people for more. This shadow of the perfect method has a chance of working in the real world, with benefits like letting humans with families and friends board together, giving airlines boarding groups they can still play with, and still being faster than the current methods.
cues.zh: 不分精确顺序，第一登机组是飞机同一侧的所有隔排。第二组是另一侧，然后往后一排，再往后一排。一、二、三、四。不能再要求人们更多了。这个完美方法的影子有机会在现实世界奏效，好处包括让带家人朋友的人一起登机，让航空公司仍有可调整的登机分组，而且仍比现行方法快。

cues.en: Reaching for perfection, we will always come up short, but perhaps we can manage to get closer in the process. Before you go, let me leave you with an annoying thought. You know how boarding a flight from front to back by row is the slowest possible method? The Reaper method? Well, after your flight, when the plane pulls into the gate and everyone ignores the flight attendant's admonishment to wait until the fasten seatbelt is off to grab their bag and the door opens, how do we deplane? That's right.
cues.zh: 追求完美，我们总会差一截，但也许过程中能更接近一点。走之前，留给你们一个烦人的念头。你知道按排从前到后登机是最慢的方法吧？死神法？那下飞机时，飞机停靠登机口，所有人无视空乘的告诫——要等安全带灯熄灭再去拿行李——门一开，我们怎么下机？没错。

cues.en: Front to back, row by row. No slower could we go.
cues.zh: 从前到后，一排一排。慢得不能再慢。
